worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the series as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{3}\frac{1}{{5}^{n-1}}={\sum }_{n=1}^{3}{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1}
$$

Since the above series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},$ it is a geometric series.

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=1,$ $r=\frac{1}{5}$ and $N=3.$ If we substitute these values into the above formula, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{3}\frac{1}{{5}^{n-1}} & =1\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{3}]}{(1-\frac{1}{5})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{124}{125})}{(\frac{4}{5})} \\  & =\frac{31}{25}\end{aligned}
$$
